entries.meaning: The outer form of something, seen as an outline. ---
examples: The cookies were cut in the shape of stars.
Draw three different shapes on the board.
That cloud has a funny shape.

entries.meaning: A perfectly round flat shape. ---
examples: The kids sat in a circle on the rug.
She drew a circle around the right answer.
Cut the dough into small circles.

entries.meaning: A flat shape with three straight sides and three angles. ---
examples: Cut each sandwich into two triangles.
The roof forms a perfect triangle.
A triangle has angles that add up to 180 degrees.

entries.meaning: A flat shape with four right angles and opposite sides of equal length. ---
examples: The screen is a wide rectangle.
Draw a rectangle twice as long as it is tall.
Most doors are simple rectangles.

entries.meaning: A shape like a slightly flattened circle, similar to an egg. ---
examples: The mirror is a tall oval.
She has a narrow face, almost a perfect oval.
The track is made of two straight lines and two ovals.

entries.meaning: A regular oval curve, like a circle seen from an angle. ---
examples: The planet moves in an ellipse around the sun.
He stretched the circle into an ellipse.
The graph showed two overlapping ellipses.

entries.meaning: Half of a circle. ---
examples: The chairs were arranged in a semicircle.
Cut the pita in half to make two semicircles.
The window above the door is a small semicircle.

entries.meaning: A flat shape with six straight sides. ---
examples: Each cell in a honeycomb is a tiny hexagon.
The floor tiles are white hexagons.
A stop sign is an octagon, not a hexagon.

entries.meaning: A flat shape with five straight sides. ---
examples: A soccer ball is covered with pentagons and hexagons.
Draw a pentagon with equal sides.
The garden plot is shaped like a pentagon.

entries.meaning: A flat shape with eight straight sides. ---
examples: A stop sign is a red octagon.
The gazebo is built as an octagon.
The kids learned to draw octagons in art class.

entries.meaning: Any flat shape made of three or more straight sides. ---
examples: A triangle is the simplest polygon.
The video game renders thousands of polygons per second.
Name each polygon by its number of sides.

entries.meaning: A flat shape with four equal sides and angles that are not right angles. ---
examples: A rhombus looks like a squashed square.
The kite is shaped like a rhombus.
Draw two rhombuses side by side.
entries.contrast: The h is silent: RAHM-bus. The plural is usually rhombuses, but the Latin plural rhombi (RAHM-by) also appears in math books.

entries.meaning: A flat four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides. ---
examples: The lampshade is shaped like a trapezoid.
Find the area of the trapezoid.
The flower bed was laid out in two trapezoids.
entries.contrast: In American English this shape is a trapezoid; in British English it is a trapezium.

entries.meaning: A perfectly round solid object, like a ball. ---
examples: The earth is not a perfect sphere.
The lamp is a frosted glass sphere.
We made spheres out of clay.

entries.meaning: A solid shape with six equal square faces. ---
examples: Drop two cubes of ice in the glass.
The box is a perfect cube.
Cut the cheese into small cubes.

entries.meaning: A solid shape with a round base that narrows to a point at the top. ---
examples: Orange cones blocked off the lane.
Roll the paper into a cone.
The mountain rises in a near-perfect cone.

entries.meaning: A solid shape with a flat base and triangular sides meeting at a point. ---
examples: The kids stacked the blocks into a pyramid.
The chart is shaped like a pyramid.
We built two paper pyramids for the science fair.

entries.meaning: A long thin mark on a surface. ---
examples: Draw a straight line from corner to corner.
Write your name on the dotted line.
The parking lines had faded away.

entries.meaning: A very small round mark. ---
examples: Her dress is navy with white dots.
From the plane the cars looked like tiny dots.
Put a dot over the i.

entries.meaning: An exact spot, or the sharp end of something. ---
examples: Mark the point where the two lines cross.
The pencil has a very sharp point.
Connect the points with a ruler.

entries.meaning: A small round mark of a different color from what is around it. ---
examples: There is a grease spot on your tie.
The puppy is white with brown spots.
I got a coffee spot on the rug.

entries.meaning: A long narrow band of color. ---
examples: His shirt has thin blue stripes.
A yellow stripe runs down the middle of the road.
Zebras have black and white stripes.

entries.meaning: A line that bends smoothly without any sharp angles. ---
examples: Slow down before the curve in the road.
The chair follows the curve of your back.
The graph shows two rising curves.

entries.meaning: A curved line that forms part of a circle. ---
examples: The ball rose in a high arc over the fence.
Draw an arc with the compass.
The sprinkler sprayed water in wide arcs.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like ark, the boat in the flood story.

entries.meaning: A place where something turns or curves. ---
examples: The cabin is just past the bend in the river.
There is a sharp bend in the pipe.
Take the next two bends slowly.

entries.meaning: A shape made when a line curves around and crosses itself. ---
examples: Make a loop with the shoelace.
Her handwriting is full of fancy loops.
The roller coaster does a full loop.

entries.meaning: A curve that winds around a center point, getting wider or tighter. ---
examples: The staircase climbs in a tight spiral.
A snail shell is a natural spiral.
She doodled little spirals in the margin.

entries.meaning: Coil has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A coil of rope hung by the door.
The heating coils glowed red.
He unwound the coil of wire.
The coil in the ignition had gone bad.
Copper coils surround the iron core.
Heat from the coil warms the water.

senses.head: A length of something wound into a series of rings
examples: A coil of rope hung by the door.
The heating coils glowed red.
He unwound the coil of wire.

senses.head: Wire wound into loops so that it makes or responds to a magnetic field
examples: The coil in the ignition had gone bad.
Copper coils surround the iron core.
Heat from the coil warms the water.

entries.meaning: A bend or turn in something long and thin. ---
examples: The path has more twists than I remembered.
Give the wire one more twist.
There is a twist in the cord behind the desk.

entries.meaning: A line that turns sharply left and right again and again. ---
examples: The trail climbs the hill in a zigzag.
Her sweater has red zigzags across the front.
Lightning cut a bright zigzag through the clouds.

entries.meaning: One of the flat surfaces or straight edges that form a shape. ---
examples: A triangle has three sides.
Write on one side of the paper only.
The box is dented on the left side.

entries.meaning: The outer line or border where something ends. ---
examples: Careful, the edge of that paper is sharp.
He sat on the edge of the bed.
Sand the rough edges smooth.

entries.meaning: The outside or top layer of something. ---
examples: Wipe the surface before you paint it.
Leaves floated on the surface of the pond.
Clean all the kitchen surfaces.

entries.meaning: Grid has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The city is laid out on a grid.
Draw a grid of nine squares.
Photos are arranged in neat grids on the page.
The heat wave pushed the grid to its limit.
Their cabin is off the grid entirely.
Texas runs its own grid, separate from the rest of the country.

senses.head: A pattern of straight lines crossing to form squares
examples: The city is laid out on a grid.
Draw a grid of nine squares.
Photos are arranged in neat grids on the page.

senses.head: The network of lines and stations that carries electricity across a region
examples: The heat wave pushed the grid to its limit.
Their cabin is off the grid entirely.
Texas runs its own grid, separate from the rest of the country.

entries.meaning: The outline or curved shape of a surface. ---
examples: The seat follows the contours of your body.
The map shows the contours of the hillside.
Sunlight brought out every contour of the rock.

entries.meaning: A long narrow cut in a surface. ---
examples: Rainwater runs down the groove in the tile.
The record has fine grooves.
Slide the panel into the groove.

entries.meaning: Crease has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Iron the crease out of the shirt.
The map has a crease right across the city.
His pants had sharp creases down the front.
His trousers had a knife-sharp crease.
The shirt came out of the suitcase full of creases.
Iron the crease back in.

senses.head: A line made in cloth or paper by folding or crushing it
examples: Iron the crease out of the shirt.
The map has a crease right across the city.
His pants had sharp creases down the front.

senses.head: A sharp line pressed into cloth, either on purpose or by accident
examples: His trousers had a knife-sharp crease.
The shirt came out of the suitcase full of creases.
Iron the crease back in.

entries.русский: складка, залом, сгиб; складка; стрелка (на брюках)

entries.meaning: A part where something is bent over onto itself. ---
examples: Press down along the fold.
The curtain hangs in soft folds.
Open the letter at the fold.

entries.meaning: A small V-shaped cut in an edge or surface. ---
examples: He cut a notch in the stick to mark the day.
Tighten the belt one notch.
There are small notches along the ruler.

entries.meaning: A hollow place in a surface where it has been hit. ---
examples: There is a dent in the car door.
The can has a big dent in the side.
Small dents covered the old toolbox.

entries.meaning: A raised round part on an otherwise flat surface. ---
examples: Slow down, there is a bump in the road.
He has a bump on his forehead.
The wall is covered with little bumps of dried paint.

entries.meaning: A thin line where something is broken but not in pieces. ---
examples: There is a crack in the windshield.
Weeds grow up through the cracks in the sidewalk.
A hairline crack runs across the plate.

entries.meaning: A rounded swelling that sticks out from a flat surface. ---
examples: There was a strange bulge in his coat pocket.
The wall has a slight bulge near the floor.
Water damage left bulges in the ceiling.

entries.meaning: Pattern has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The wallpaper has a floral pattern.
I like the tile, but not the pattern.
The store sells fabric in dozens of patterns.
Pin the pattern to the fabric before you cut.
She bought a pattern for a summer dress.
The two fabrics have very similar patterns.

senses.head: A design of shapes or colors that repeats
examples: The wallpaper has a floral pattern.
I like the tile, but not the pattern.
The store sells fabric in dozens of patterns.

senses.head: A paper shape used to cut out the pieces of a garment, or a design on cloth
examples: Pin the pattern to the fabric before you cut.
She bought a pattern for a summer dress.
The two fabrics have very similar patterns.

entries.meaning: Plaid has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He always wears a red flannel plaid.
The blanket is a soft green plaid.
The store had plaids in every color.
Every guy in the room had on a plaid shirt.
She bought two yards of green plaid.
The store was full of loud plaids.

senses.head: A pattern of crossing colored stripes forming squares
examples: He always wears a red flannel plaid.
The blanket is a soft green plaid.
The store had plaids in every color.

senses.head: Cloth woven with crossing bands of color in a checked pattern
examples: Every guy in the room had on a plaid shirt.
She bought two yards of green plaid.
The store was full of loud plaids.

entries.русский: шотландка, клетчатый узор; клетчатая ткань, шотландка
entries.contrast: Spelled with ai but pronounced PLAD, rhyming with sad.

entries.meaning: One of a pattern of evenly spaced round dots on cloth. ---
examples: Her blouse is covered in white polka dots.
I bought a red dress with black polka dots.
Each polka dot is about the size of a dime.
entries.contrast: In American speech the l is usually silent here: POH-kuh dot, not POHL-kuh.

entries.meaning: A board or pattern of alternating light and dark squares. ---
examples: The kitchen floor is a black and white checkerboard.
He set up the checkerboard on the porch.
The quilt is made of two checkerboards sewn together.
entries.contrast: American spelling; the British write chequerboard.

entries.meaning: A twisting curved pattern or movement. ---
examples: The ice cream has a swirl of caramel in it.
Paint the wall with light swirls.
A swirl of dust rose off the road.

entries.meaning: Material made of threads or wires with small open spaces between them. ---
examples: The screen door is fine wire mesh.
Onions come in a plastic mesh bag.
The sports shirt has mesh panels under the arms.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: A smooth change from one color or shade to another. ---
examples: The background is a blue gradient.
Add a soft gradient behind the title.
The poster uses two overlapping gradients.

entries.meaning: A pattern or arrangement of lines and shapes made for decoration. ---
examples: The rug has a simple geometric design.
She painted a design on the mailbox.
The mugs come in four designs.
entries.contrast: The g is silent: dih-ZYNE, never dih-ZIG-n.

entries.meaning: Red, blue, green and so on, or the quality that makes things look that way. ---
examples: What color is your new car?
The garden is full of color in June.
The shirt comes in six colors.
entries.countability: both — countable and uncountable with different meanings
entries.contrast: American spelling; the British write colour.

entries.meaning: The color of blood and ripe tomatoes. ---
examples: Red is her favorite color.
The painting uses several deep reds.
That bright red is hard to miss.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like read in the past tense, as in I read the book yesterday.

entries.meaning: The color of a clear sky. ---
examples: The walls are painted a soft blue.
He likes dark blues and grays.
Blue looks good on you.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like blew, the past tense of blow.

entries.meaning: The color of grass and leaves. ---
examples: The kitchen is a pale green.
The hills show a dozen shades of green.
She mixed two greens to get the right tone.

entries.meaning: The color of lemons and school buses. ---
examples: The front door is a bright yellow.
Yellow shows dirt easily.
The room is decorated in soft yellows.

entries.meaning: The color made by mixing red and blue. ---
examples: Her bedroom is a deep purple.
Purple was the color of kings.
The sunset turned through several purples.

entries.meaning: A pale red color, like that of many roses. ---
examples: She painted her nails a bright pink.
The sky faded from orange to pink.
The catalog shows four different pinks.

entries.meaning: The color of chocolate, coffee, or soil. ---
examples: The couch is a warm brown.
The forest is all browns and grays in November.
Brown hides stains well.

entries.meaning: The darkest color, the opposite of white. ---
examples: She always wears black to work.
The photo is in black and white.
The printer is out of black.

entries.meaning: The lightest color, like fresh snow. ---
examples: The trim is painted a clean white.
Wash the whites separately.
White makes the room look bigger.

entries.meaning: The color between black and white, like storm clouds. ---
examples: The sky was a flat gray all day.
He picked a soft gray for the hallway.
The paint chips show a dozen grays.
entries.contrast: Americans spell it gray; the British spell it grey.

entries.meaning: A pale sandy brown color. ---
examples: The whole office is painted beige.
She wore a coat in soft beige.
Beige is safe but a little boring.
entries.contrast: Ends in the zh sound of measure, not a hard j: BAYZH.

entries.meaning: A light yellowish brown, or the browner skin color you get from the sun. ---
examples: He wore tan pants and a blue shirt.
She came back from Florida with a deep tan.
The store carries the shoe in two tans.

entries.meaning: A dark brownish red. ---
examples: The school colors are maroon and gold.
She bought a scarf in deep maroon.
The seats are covered in maroon velvet.

entries.meaning: A deep rich red. ---
examples: The maple leaves turned a brilliant crimson.
She blushed crimson.
The banner is crimson with white letters.

entries.meaning: A bright red with a slight orange tone. ---
examples: The cardinal is a flash of scarlet in the snow.
She wore scarlet to the party.
The poppies were a solid field of scarlet.

entries.meaning: A dark blue-green color. ---
examples: The bathroom tile is a soft teal.
I love that jacket in teal.
Teal looks good next to gray.

entries.meaning: A bright purplish pink. ---
examples: The printer is low on magenta.
The flowers are a shocking magenta.
She highlighted the text in magenta.

entries.meaning: A deep blue color with a hint of violet. ---
examples: Real jeans are dyed with indigo.
The sky over the desert was pure indigo.
The scarf is indigo with silver thread.

entries.meaning: A dull yellowish green. ---
examples: The jacket comes in black or olive.
The walls were painted a muddy olive.
Olive was everywhere in military clothing.

entries.meaning: Khaki has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He showed up in khaki and a polo shirt.
The tent is khaki so it blends in.
I keep two pairs of khakis for work.
The uniform was plain khaki.
He wore khakis and a blue blazer.
My khakis need to go to the cleaners.

senses.head: A dull yellowish brown, often used for uniforms and pants
examples: He showed up in khaki and a polo shirt.
The tent is khaki so it blends in.
I keep two pairs of khakis for work.

senses.head: A dull yellowish-brown cotton cloth, or in the plural, pants made from it
body: (хаки (ткань и цвет); мн. ч. брюки цвета хаки)
examples: The uniform was plain khaki.
He wore khakis and a blue blazer.
My khakis need to go to the cleaners.

entries.русский: хаки (жёлто-коричневый цвет); хаки (ткань и цвет); мн. ч. брюки цвета хаки
entries.contrast: Americans say KAK-ee; the British say KAH-kee. In the plural, khakis usually means khaki pants.

entries.meaning: A deep purplish red, like red wine. ---
examples: The couch is a rich burgundy.
She chose burgundy for the bridesmaid dresses.
His tie is burgundy with thin stripes.

entries.meaning: A greenish blue, one of the basic printing colors. ---
examples: The cyan cartridge is empty.
Printers mix cyan, magenta, yellow, and black.
The logo is a bright cyan.

entries.meaning: A woman or girl with light-colored hair. ---
examples: She is a natural blonde.
Two blondes were sitting at the next table.
My sister was a blonde until she was ten.
entries.contrast: Blonde with an e usually describes a woman; blond without it is used for men and for hair color in general.

entries.meaning: A woman or girl with dark brown hair. ---
examples: She was a tall brunette in a red coat.
Both brunettes were on the swim team.
He always said he preferred brunettes.

entries.meaning: A small amount of a color added to something, making it lighter. ---
examples: The white paint has a pink tint.
The windows have a gray tint.
Choose from four tints of gray.

entries.meaning: A shade of a color, especially how light or dark it is. ---
examples: The room is done in warm earth tones.
Pick a tone that matches your skin.
The photo has a bluish tone.

entries.meaning: How much light something gives off or reflects. ---
examples: Turn down the brightness on your screen.
The brightness of the snow hurt my eyes.
You can adjust the brightness in the settings.

entries.meaning: A soft steady light, or a warm color in someone's face. ---
examples: A faint glow came from under the door.
Her cheeks had a healthy glow.
The city gave off an orange glow all night.

entries.meaning: The bright look of a smooth clean surface. ---
examples: The floor has a beautiful shine.
Rain took the shine right off the car.
Buff the table to bring back its shine.

entries.meaning: A smooth shiny finish on a surface. ---
examples: The paint dries to a high gloss.
Her hair had a beautiful gloss.
We chose gloss rather than flat for the trim.

entries.meaning: A soft gentle shine on a surface. ---
examples: The silk has a lovely sheen.
There was a sheen of sweat on his forehead.
Wax gives the wood a warm sheen.

entries.meaning: Luster has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The old coins have lost their luster.
Real pearls have a deep luster.
The conditioner brings back the hair's luster.
Silk has a luster that polyester can't match.
The fabric loses its luster after a few washes.
Mercerized cotton has more luster.

senses.head: The soft glowing shine of something like a pearl or polished metal
examples: The old coins have lost their luster.
Real pearls have a deep luster.
The conditioner brings back the hair's luster.

senses.head: The soft shine on the surface of a fabric or fiber
examples: Silk has a luster that polyester can't match.
The fabric loses its luster after a few washes.
Mercerized cotton has more luster.

entries.contrast: American spelling; the British write lustre.

entries.meaning: Bright flashing points of light coming off a surface. ---
examples: The diamond lost none of its sparkle.
There was a sparkle in her eyes.
Fresh snow has a sparkle in the morning sun.

entries.meaning: Tiny shiny pieces used for decoration, or the light they throw off. ---
examples: The card was covered in gold glitter.
There is glitter all over the kitchen table.
The dress caught the light with a soft glitter.

entries.meaning: Light that is too bright to look at, or a long angry look. ---
examples: The glare off the water was blinding.
She gave me a cold glare and walked away.
The new screen cuts down on glare.
entries.countability: both — countable and uncountable with different meanings

entries.meaning: A shape that cannot be seen clearly because its edges are not sharp. ---
examples: Without my glasses everything is a blur.
The car went by in a red blur.
The photo shows two gray blurs in the background.

entries.meaning: The quality of letting light through so you can see the other side. ---
examples: The glaze keeps the transparency of the glass.
Reduce the transparency of that layer.
The plastic loses its transparency over time.

entries.meaning: The quality of not letting light through. ---
examples: Set the opacity to fifty percent.
Two coats of paint give better opacity.
The fabric has enough opacity for a curtain.

entries.meaning: The way someone or something looks. ---
examples: He cares a lot about his appearance.
The house has a neglected appearance.
Do not judge people by appearances.

entries.meaning: The particular appearance or style of a person or thing. ---
examples: She has a very natural look.
White paint gave the room a fresh look.
The band tried out several different looks.

entries.meaning: The fact of looking like someone or something else. ---
examples: There is a strong resemblance between the two brothers.
She bears a striking resemblance to her grandmother.
The drawing has no resemblance to the real building.

entries.meaning: The look on someone's face that shows what they feel. ---
examples: She had a puzzled expression.
His expression never changed.
The photos catch a whole range of expressions.

entries.meaning: The general size and shape of a person's body. ---
examples: He has a slim build.
The suspect was of medium build.
The brothers have completely different builds.

entries.meaning: The shape and condition of a person's body, especially a muscular one. ---
examples: Years of swimming gave him a powerful physique.
She has the physique of a dancer.
The magazine is full of impossible physiques.
entries.contrast: The ending -que is just a k sound: fih-ZEEK, not fih-ZEE-kwee.

entries.meaning: The way you hold your body when you stand or sit. ---
examples: Sitting all day is bad for your posture.
She has excellent posture.
The trainer worked on his posture first.

entries.meaning: A person's natural height. ---
examples: He is small in stature but very strong.
Her stature made her easy to spot in a crowd.
Jockeys tend to be short in stature.

entries.meaning: The way someone's hair is cut and arranged. ---
examples: She changed her hairstyle over the summer.
That hairstyle really suits you.
The magazine shows hairstyles from the seventies.

entries.meaning: The act of having your hair cut, or the style that results. ---
examples: I need a haircut before the wedding.
Nice haircut, by the way.
Haircuts are twenty dollars at that place.

entries.meaning: Hair cut straight across the forehead. ---
examples: She cut her own bangs again.
His bangs keep falling into his eyes.
I am growing out my bangs.
entries.contrast: Americans say bangs and always in the plural; the British call the same thing a fringe.

entries.meaning: Hair tied together at the back of the head so it hangs down. ---
examples: She pulled her hair back into a ponytail.
He runs with his hair in a ponytail.
The girls wore matching ponytails.

entries.meaning: Hair growing down the sides of a man's face in front of his ears. ---
examples: He grew long sideburns in college.
The barber trimmed his sideburns.
Those sideburns look very seventies.

entries.meaning: Short hair on a man's face when he has not shaved for a day or two. ---
examples: He had two days of stubble on his chin.
The stubble scratched her cheek.
A little stubble actually looks good on him.

entries.meaning: A piece of hair that grows or is shaped in a curve. ---
examples: A loose curl fell across her forehead.
The baby has soft blond curls.
The rain took the curl right out of my hair.

entries.meaning: Braid has 2 distinct senses.
examples: She wears her hair in a long braid.
Mom put my hair in two braids for school.
The braid came loose during practice.
The uniform had gold braid on the cuffs.
She wore her hair in two braids.
Sew the braid along the hem.

senses.head: Hair divided into three parts and woven together
examples: She wears her hair in a long braid.
Mom put my hair in two braids for school.
The braid came loose during practice.

senses.head: Narrow woven trim sewn onto clothing, or a length of hair plaited together
examples: The uniform had gold braid on the cuffs.
She wore her hair in two braids.
Sew the braid along the hem.

entries.contrast: Americans say braid; the British usually say plait, pronounced PLAT.

entries.meaning: A small mark that spoils the look of skin or a surface. ---
examples: The cream is supposed to hide blemishes.
The table is perfect except for one small blemish.
There was not a single blemish on the fruit.

entries.meaning: A thin shallow mark cut into a surface or the skin. ---
examples: There is a scratch on the hood of my car.
The cat left three scratches on his arm.
The screen has a tiny scratch in the corner.

entries.meaning: A small fault that keeps something from being perfect. ---
examples: The diamond has one tiny flaw.
I could not find a single flaw in the finish.
The fabric has a few flaws in the weave.

entries.meaning: A long thin line of a different color from what is around it. ---
examples: She has gray streaks in her hair.
There are dirty streaks on the window.
A streak of light crossed the ceiling.

entries.meaning: A dirty mark made by rubbing something. ---
examples: There is an ink smudge on the last page.
Her glasses were covered in smudges.
He wiped the smudge off the screen.

entries.meaning: A very small spot or piece of something. ---
examples: There is a speck of dirt on your collar.
Specks of paint covered his hands.
The boat was just a speck on the horizon.

entries.meaning: A spot or line on a surface that spoils its appearance.
examples: The glass left a ring mark on the wood.
There were muddy marks all over the floor.
The burn left a small mark on her arm.
